title: The Whole Bakery
premise: Ada Brightwater, a wedding planner whose own marriage ended in a courthouse hallway, is hired to plan a harvest festival at Hollow Orchard — only to discover the deed lists two names: hers, inherited from the grandmother she never thanked, and Jonah Reyes, the boy she abandoned fifteen years ago to save her family from debt. As the orchard's first harvest approaches, their forced partnership thaws into something neither trusts, until Ada uncovers that Jonah's vineyard career was built on quietly buying out her grandmother's failing loans. At the harvest festival, Ada must choose between exposing the truth and keeping him; she chooses truth, and Jonah, given the choice between the career that saved him and the woman who finally sees him whole, signs his half of the deed over to her — then stays anyway, not as co-owner but as the man who learned that survival isn't the same as living.
about_author: Lior Delacroix spent six years coordinating weddings in wine country before trading clipboards for manuscripts, and still cries at vows even though they no longer believe in them. They write romances about people who mistake endurance for love, from a farmhouse with an orchard out back.

chapters.title: The Deed and the Debt
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Hired to stage Hollow Orchard's first harvest festival, Ada discovers her grandmother's name beside a stranger's on the deed — then learns the stranger is Jonah Reyes, the boy she left behind when her family fled their debts. The emotional beat is dread braided with longing: she came to plan someone else's celebration and found her own unfinished story waiting in the rows of unripe grapes.

chapters.title: Frost Warnings
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Forced to collaborate, Ada and Jonah circle each other through frost blankets and festival budgets, old wounds surfacing in small cruelties and smaller kindnesses. A late-night power outage in the packing house nearly becomes a confession — until Jonah deflects. The beat is rising tension: proximity is thawing them both, but Ada notices he flinches whenever money or the deed comes up.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Digging through her grandmother's records for the festival, Ada finds loan documents showing Jonah quietly bought the orchard's debts years ago — the inheritance she's mourning was saved by the man she betrayed, who never told her. Confronted, he admits he built his whole career on this land and this secret. The climax beat: Ada must decide whether loyalty to her grandmother's memory means exposing him publicly at the festival or forgiving what survival made him do.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the festival, Ada tells the crowd the orchard's true history — including his name — choosing truth over protection. Certain he's lost everything, Jonah offers her his half of the deed; instead she asks why he stayed all these years. His answer — that some things you save because you can't stop loving them — lands as the first grapes come in. Resolution beat: they press the season's first cider together, co-owners of the past at last.
